body.alt: Five signs to skip the pharmacy and go straight to an emergency room: difficulty breathing, chest pain or pressure, neurological changes such as slurred speech, severe pain or injury, and any fever in an infant under three months

Five signs a burn needs emergency care: it is on the face, hands, feet or a major joint, it is larger than three inches, blisters are numerous or the pain is unmanageable, it is chemical or electrical, or there is difficulty breathing after a fire

Early dehydration signs in adult fans against young fans: extreme thirst and a dry mouth against a dry tongue and lips, dark urine against fewer than six wet diapers, fatigue or brain fog against listlessness or irritability, and dizziness against no tears when crying

A carbon monoxide alarm checklist: place one on every level of the home and one right outside every sleeping area, then test each alarm monthly, change the batteries every six months and replace the unit after five to seven years

The first three steps after a workplace injury: call 911 for heavy bleeding or loss of consciousness, get driven to an ER for serious injuries that are not life-threatening, and report the injury to your employer in writing

Three reasons gout attacks begin between midnight and 8 AM: body temperature drops and uric acid is less soluble when cooler, overnight fluid loss concentrates uric acid, and cortisol is at its lowest

Four things untreated dehydration can lead to: electrolyte imbalance affecting heart rhythm, heat exhaustion or heat stroke above 104 degrees Fahrenheit, kidney strain that can cause stones or acute injury, and hypovolemic shock
